title: In the Vision, the Prophet Directs Babur Back to Guru Nanak

blocks.text: In the narrative’s visionary scene, the Prophet answers Babur without ambiguity: sovereignty over India belongs to Guru Nanak, not to him, and Babur should seek that favor from the Guru instead. He can promise rule in Khorasan and for the Timurid line, but not dominion over Hindustan.

The refusal leaves Babur shaken and ashamed, because he has returned from heaven without the prize he wanted most. His body trembles, his confidence collapses, and he can see no easy path either back to the prophet or onward into battle.

Caught between dread and ambition, Babur sinks into anxious reflection over how he can cross this ordeal at all. The page ends with him in spiritual crisis, searching for a way to approach the one authority who can still help him.
